//: For the editor and for `tsc --noEmit` only — nothing is ever built from this. Plain `node` runs the
.ts files directly by stripping types at load.
Extends ../tsconfig.base.json, which is the SAME file as sdk/js-sdk/tsconfig.base.json (the source
of truth). It used to restate its own options and had drifted badly: noUncheckedIndexedAccess and
exactOptionalPropertyTypes were off, skipLibCheck was on, target/lib were ahead, and eleven flags
were simply absent. Extending rather than restating is what stops that happening again.
The overrides below are the whole exception list, and each is forced rather than chosen:
types            base is [] so the published payload cannot reach Node APIs; this IS a node
script, so it needs them (same override as internal/tsconfig.json)
rootDir          base says `src`, which does not exist here
noEmit           nothing is emitted, and it is what allowImportingTsExtensions requires
allowImportingTs the source says `./utils.ts`, which node requires for relative imports and tsc
erasableSyntax   fails the typecheck on anything node cannot strip (enum, namespace, parameter
Only             properties), so the editor catches it before node does
`include` is a GLOB on purpose. A named file list only checked files something imported, so common.ts
was covered solely because deploy-testnet.ts pulled it in — and a new module nobody imports yet would
have been checked by nothing at all.
